items.stem: State any three factors affecting the value of goodwill.
items.answer: Nature of business; Location; Efficiency of management; Market situation; Special advantages; Quality of products
items.markingKey: Any three of: Nature of business; Location; Efficiency of management; Market situation; Special advantages; Quality of products (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about goodwill is correct?
items.answer: Goodwill arises from the ability to earn super profits.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Goodwill arises from the ability to earn super profits.
options: A firm earning only normal profit has a large goodwill.
Goodwill is a fictitious asset.
Goodwill is valued only at the time of dissolution.
Goodwill arises from the ability to earn super profits.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Goodwill is a fictitious asset.
Reason (R): Goodwill can be sold only along with the business.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: goodwill is intangible, not fictitious. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Profits of the last three years are given weights 1, 2 and 3 and the result is multiplied by 2. Which method of valuing goodwill is being used?
items.answer: Weighted average profit method
items.markingKey: (d) Weighted average profit method. Weights are applied because profits show a trend.
options: Average profit method
Capitalisation of average profit method
Super profit method
Weighted average profit method

items.stem: The average profit is capitalised at the normal rate of return and the net assets are deducted from it. Which method of valuing goodwill is being used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Capitalisation of average profit method. Capitalised value of average profit − net assets.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Capitalisation of average profit method; 2 marks for the justification: Capitalised value of average profit − net assets.

items.stem: Which method of valuing goodwill is being used? In each case give a reason. (i) Profits of the last three years are given weights 1, 2 and 3 and the result is multiplied by 2. (ii) The average profit is capitalised at the normal rate of return and the net assets are deducted from it.
items.answer: (i) Weighted average profit method: Weights are applied because profits show a trend. (ii) Capitalisation of average profit method: Capitalised value of average profit − net assets.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Weighted average profit method (ii) Capitalisation of average profit method

items.stem: A firm has capital employed of ₹5,70,000 and an average profit of ₹1,24,500. The normal rate of return is 15%. Calculate goodwill by capitalising the super profit.

Profits of a firm were 2022-23 ₹77,000, 2023-24 ₹94,000, 2024-25 ₹1,46,000, 2025-26 loss ₹6,000. The profit of 2023-24 includes the effect of an abnormal gain of ₹11,000. Calculate goodwill at 2 years' purchase of the average profit.
Calculate the goodwill of a firm at 4 years' purchase of the average profit of the last 4 years. Profits: 2022-23 ₹1,34,000, 2023-24 ₹84,000, 2024-25 ₹69,000, 2025-26 ₹55,000.
Calculate the goodwill of a firm at 5/2 years' purchase of the average profit of the last 4 years. Profits: 2022-23 ₹89,000, 2023-24 ₹89,000, 2024-25 ₹1,28,000, 2025-26 ₹1,21,000.

Profits of a firm were 2022-23 ₹88,000, 2023-24 ₹1,24,000, 2024-25 ₹1,28,000, 2025-26 ₹1,54,000. The profit of 2024-25 includes the effect of an abnormal loss of ₹5,000. Calculate goodwill at 2 years' purchase of the average profit.
Explain the following factors affecting the value of goodwill: (i) Special advantages (ii) Location.
items.answer: (i) Special advantages: Import licences, patents, trademarks or a long-term contract raise goodwill. (ii) Location: A centrally located business attracts more customers.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Import licences, patents, trademarks or a long-term contract raise goodwill. (ii) A centrally located business attracts more customers.

items.stem: Profits of a firm for three years were 2023-24 ₹1,28,000, 2024-25 ₹1,46,000, 2025-26 ₹1,67,000 (weights 1, 2 and 3 respectively). Calculate goodwill at 3 years' purchase of the weighted average profit.
State any three rights acquired by a new partner on admission.
items.answer: Right to share the assets of the firm; Right to share future profits; Right to take part in the business
items.markingKey: Any three of: Right to share the assets of the firm; Right to share future profits; Right to take part in the business (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about admission of a partner is correct?
items.answer: Sacrificing ratio = Old ratio − New ratio.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Sacrificing ratio = Old ratio − New ratio.
options: The old firm is dissolved on admission of a partner.
The sacrificing ratio is always the old ratio.
Sacrificing ratio = Old ratio − New ratio.
Sacrificing ratio = New ratio − Old ratio.

items.stem: Explain the following adjustments required at the time of admission of a partner: (i) Adjustment of capitals (ii) Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities.
items.answer: (i) Adjustment of capitals: Capitals may be made proportionate to the new ratio. (ii) Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities: Gains or losses up to admission belong to old partners.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Capitals may be made proportionate to the new ratio. (ii) Gains or losses up to admission belong to old partners.

items.stem: Priya and Tara share profits 5:3. Dev is admitted for a 1/6 share, which Dev acquires equally from Priya and Tara. The new profit-sharing ratio of Priya, Tara and Dev is:
items.markingKey: (a) New shares: Priya 13/24, Tara 7/24, Dev 1/6 → 13:7:4.

items.stem: Kavya and Diya share profits in the ratio 3:1. Kunal is admitted for a 1/3 share, taken from Kavya and Diya in their old ratio. Calculate the new profit-sharing ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
items.answer: New ratio 3:1:2; sacrificing ratio 3:1
items.markingKey: New shares: Kavya 1/2, Diya 1/6, Kunal 1/3 = 3:1:2 (2 marks). Sacrifice = old − new: Kavya 1/4, Diya 1/12 = 3:1 (1 mark).

items.stem: Siddharth and Priya share profits in the ratio 5:3. Harleen is admitted; Harleen acquires 1/6 of the profit from Siddharth and 1/10 from Priya. Calculate the new profit-sharing ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
items.answer: New ratio 55:33:32; sacrificing ratio 5:3
items.markingKey: New shares: Siddharth 11/24, Priya 11/40, Harleen 4/15 = 55:33:32 (2 marks). Sacrifice = old − new: Siddharth 1/6, Priya 1/10 = 5:3 (1 mark).

items.stem: Harleen and Ananya share profits 3:5. Rohan is admitted; Rohan acquires 1/6 of the profit from Harleen and 1/8 from Ananya. The sacrificing ratio of Harleen and Ananya is:
items.markingKey: (b) Sacrifice = old share − new share: 1/6 and 1/8 → 4:3.

items.stem: Lakshmi and Dev share profits 7:3. Varun is admitted for a 1/3 share, which Varun acquires equally from Lakshmi and Dev. The sacrificing ratio of Lakshmi and Dev is:
items.markingKey: (d) Sacrifice = old share − new share: 1/6 and 1/6 → 1:1.

items.stem: State any three adjustments required at the time of admission of a partner.
items.answer: New profit-sharing ratio and sacrificing ratio; Valuation and treatment of goodwill; Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities; Distribution of accumulated profits and reserves; Adjustment of capitals
items.markingKey: Any three of: New profit-sharing ratio and sacrificing ratio; Valuation and treatment of goodwill; Revaluation of assets and reassessment of liabilities; Distribution of accumulated profits and reserves; Adjustment of capitals (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Existing goodwill"?
items.answer: Goodwill already appearing in the books of the old firm, written off among old partners in the old ratio on admission.
items.markingKey: (d) Existing goodwill: Goodwill already appearing in the books of the old firm, written off among old partners in the old ratio on admission.
options: Goodwill inferred from the capital brought by the new partner when the firm's goodwill is not given.
The amount brought by the new partner in cash as compensation to the old partners for their sacrifice.
The accounting standard under which only purchased goodwill is recorded in the books; self-generated goodwill is not.
Goodwill already appearing in the books of the old firm, written off among old partners in the old ratio on admission.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about treatment of goodwill on admission is correct?
items.answer: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
options: Premium for goodwill is credited to the new partner.
Goodwill account is always opened at full value on admission.
Premium for goodwill is credited to all partners in the new ratio.
Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Goodwill account is raised in the books on the admission of a partner.
Reason (R): AS 26 allows only purchased goodwill to be recorded.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: goodwill is not raised on admission. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Aisha is admitted but is unable to bring her share of goodwill in cash. Which journal entry records this?
items.answer: New partner's Current A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs
items.markingKey: (d) New partner's Current A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs. The new partner's current (or capital) account is debited and sacrificing partners credited.
options: Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c
Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c
Goodwill A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs
New partner's Current A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs

items.stem: Goodwill of ₹60,000 already appears in the books when Karthik is admitted. Which journal entry records this? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c. Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c; 2 marks for the justification: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.

items.stem: Which journal entry records this? In each case give a reason. (i) Goodwill of ₹60,000 already appears in the books when Dev is admitted. (ii) Dev is admitted and brings his share of goodwill in cash.
items.answer: (i) Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio. (ii) Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c: Cash brought for goodwill is first credited to Premium for Goodwill.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c (ii) Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c

items.stem: Vihaan and Tara have capitals of ₹2,50,000 and ₹50,000 after all adjustments. Aisha is admitted for a 1/5 share and brings ₹1,60,000 as capital. Calculate the hidden goodwill of the firm.
items.markingKey: Total capital of new firm on the basis of Aisha's capital = ₹1,60,000 × 5 = ₹8,00,000; actual combined capital = ₹3,00,000 + ₹1,60,000 = ₹4,60,000; goodwill = ₹3,40,000.

items.stem: Gauri and Yash share profits 4:3. Karthik is admitted for a 1/5 share, which Karthik acquires equally from Gauri and Yash. The firm's goodwill is valued at ₹4,14,000. Karthik brings the share of goodwill in cash. Pass the journal entries.
items.answer: Bank A/c Dr ₹82,800; To Premium for Goodwill A/c ₹82,800. Premium for Goodwill A/c Dr ₹82,800; To Gauri's Capital A/c ₹41,400; To Yash's Capital A/c ₹41,400
items.markingKey: Karthik's share of goodwill = ₹4,14,000 × 1/5 = ₹82,800; sacrificing ratio 1:1; Gauri ₹41,400, Yash ₹41,400. Entries: Bank A/c Dr ₹82,800; To Premium for Goodwill A/c ₹82,800. Premium for Goodwill A/c Dr ₹82,800; To Gauri's Capital A/c ₹41,400; To Yash's Capital A/c ₹41,400.

items.stem: What is meant by "AS 26 (Intangible Assets)"?
items.answer: The accounting standard under which only purchased goodwill is recorded in the books; self-generated goodwill is not.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The accounting standard under which only purchased goodwill is recorded in the books; self-generated goodwill is not.

items.stem: Karthik and Aarav share profits 5:3. Karthik surrenders 1/3 of Karthik's share and Aarav surrenders 1/3 of Aarav's share in favour of Sneha, the new partner. Goodwill of the firm is ₹1,68,000 and Sneha brings the share of goodwill in cash. The premium will be credited to:
items.answer: Karthik ₹35,000, Aarav ₹21,000
items.markingKey: (c) Premium ₹56,000 shared in sacrificing ratio 5:3.
options: Karthik ₹21,000, Aarav ₹35,000
Karthik ₹1,05,000, Aarav ₹63,000
Karthik ₹35,000, Aarav ₹21,000
Karthik ₹28,000, Aarav ₹28,000

items.stem: Sahil and Vihaan share profits 2:3. Imran is admitted; Imran acquires 1/5 of the profit from Sahil and 1/10 from Vihaan. Goodwill of the firm is ₹1,02,000 and Imran brings the share of goodwill in cash. The premium will be credited to:
items.answer: Sahil ₹20,400, Vihaan ₹10,200
items.markingKey: (c) Premium ₹30,600 shared in sacrificing ratio 2:1.
options: Sahil ₹40,800, Vihaan ₹61,200
Sahil ₹12,240, Vihaan ₹18,360
Sahil ₹20,400, Vihaan ₹10,200
Sahil ₹15,300, Vihaan ₹15,300

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Investment Fluctuation Reserve"?
items.answer: A reserve created to meet a fall in the value of investments; any excess over the fall belongs to old partners.
items.markingKey: (c) Investment Fluctuation Reserve: A reserve created to meet a fall in the value of investments; any excess over the fall belongs to old partners.
options: Undistributed profits such as general reserve and profit and loss (credit) balance, belonging to the old partners.
A reserve created for claims of workmen; any excess over the actual claim is distributed among old partners.
A reserve created to meet a fall in the value of investments; any excess over the fall belongs to old partners.
A nominal account prepared on reconstitution to record changes in the values of assets and liabilities and find the gain or loss.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about revaluation on admission is correct?
items.answer: Revaluation gain is shared by old partners in the old ratio.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Revaluation gain is shared by old partners in the old ratio.
options: The new partner bears a share of revaluation loss.
General reserve is credited to the Revaluation Account.
Decrease in an asset is credited to the Revaluation Account.
Revaluation gain is shared by old partners in the old ratio.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about revaluation on admission is NOT correct?
items.answer: General reserve is credited to the Revaluation Account.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: General reserve is credited to the Revaluation Account.
options: General reserve is credited to the Revaluation Account.
Revaluation gain is shared by old partners in the old ratio.
Unrecorded assets are credited to the Revaluation Account.
Increase in a liability is debited to the Revaluation Account.

items.stem: Building is to be appreciated by 10%. Which side of the Revaluation Account is affected?
items.answer: Credit side (gain)
items.markingKey: (a) Credit side (gain). An increase in an asset is a gain.
options: Credit side (gain)
Not shown in Revaluation Account
Both sides equally
Debit side (loss)

items.stem: Shreya and Kabir share profits 3:2. On Aryan's admission their balance sheet shows general reserve ₹84,000, profit and loss account (credit) ₹31,000 and workmen compensation reserve ₹35,000. The workmen compensation claim is ₹26,000. Calculate the amount credited (or debited) to each old partner's capital account for these items.
items.answer: Net ₹1,24,000 credited: Shreya ₹74,400, Kabir ₹49,600
items.markingKey: General reserve ₹84,000 + P&L ₹31,000 + excess WCR ₹9,000 = ₹1,24,000; old ratio 3:2: Shreya ₹74,400, Kabir ₹49,600.

items.stem: Yash and Siddharth share profits 3:2. On Aisha's admission their balance sheet shows general reserve ₹15,000, profit and loss account (credit) ₹21,000 and workmen compensation reserve ₹30,000. The workmen compensation claim is ₹21,000. Calculate the amount credited (or debited) to each old partner's capital account for these items.
items.answer: Net ₹45,000 credited: Yash ₹27,000, Siddharth ₹18,000
items.markingKey: General reserve ₹15,000 + P&L ₹21,000 + excess WCR ₹9,000 = ₹45,000; old ratio 3:2: Yash ₹27,000, Siddharth ₹18,000.

items.stem: On the admission of a partner: (1) An outstanding electricity bill of ₹5,500 is unrecorded; (2) Machinery (₹2,20,000) is depreciated by 5%; (3) Creditors (₹1,35,000) include an amount of ₹5,000 not payable. The result of revaluation is:
items.answer: Loss of ₹11,500
options: Gain of ₹5,000
Loss of ₹11,500
Gain of ₹11,500
Gain of ₹21,500

items.stem: Zoya and Rahul share profits 2:3. On admitting Dev, it was agreed: (1) An outstanding electricity bill of ₹4,500 is unrecorded; (2) A provision for doubtful debts @ 10% is created on debtors of ₹60,000; (3) Stock is overvalued by ₹3,000; (4) Creditors (₹1,15,000) include an amount of ₹4,500 not payable; (5) An unrecorded investment worth ₹13,000 is to be brought into books. Prepare the Revaluation Account and show the gain credited or debited to each old partner.
items.answer: Revaluation gain ₹4,000: Zoya ₹1,600, Rahul ₹2,400
items.markingKey: Items: (1) loss ₹4,500; (2) loss ₹6,000; (3) loss ₹3,000; (4) gain ₹4,500; (5) gain ₹13,000. Net gain ₹4,000 (3 marks for items), shared by old partners in old ratio 2:3: Zoya ₹1,600, Rahul ₹2,400 (1 mark).

items.stem: Arjun and Farhan share profits 1:1. On admitting Aryan, it was agreed: (1) Building (₹3,50,000) is appreciated by 10%; (2) Prepaid insurance of ₹1,000 is to be recorded; (3) Creditors (₹1,15,000) include an amount of ₹2,000 not payable; (4) A provision for doubtful debts @ 2% is created on debtors of ₹1,70,000. Prepare the Revaluation Account and show the gain credited or debited to each old partner.
items.answer: Revaluation gain ₹34,600: Arjun ₹17,300, Farhan ₹17,300
items.markingKey: Items: (1) gain ₹35,000; (2) gain ₹1,000; (3) gain ₹2,000; (4) loss ₹3,400. Net gain ₹34,600 (3 marks for items), shared by old partners in old ratio 1:1: Arjun ₹17,300, Farhan ₹17,300 (1 mark).

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Adjusted capital"?
items.answer: A partner's capital after all adjustments for goodwill, revaluation and reserves.
items.markingKey: (a) Adjusted capital: A partner's capital after all adjustments for goodwill, revaluation and reserves.
options: A partner's capital after all adjustments for goodwill, revaluation and reserves.
Capital of partners adjusted so that it is in the same proportion as their new profit-sharing ratio.
The excess of a partner's adjusted capital over the required capital, withdrawn or transferred to current account.
The shortfall of a partner's adjusted capital from the required capital, brought in cash or debited to current account.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about adjustment of capitals on admission is correct?
items.answer: Surplus capital may be transferred to current account.
items.markingKey: (c) Correct: Surplus capital may be transferred to current account.
options: Surplus capital is credited to the Revaluation Account.
The new partner's capital is always equal to the old partners' total.
Surplus capital may be transferred to current account.
Capitals are always adjusted in the old ratio.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about adjustment of capitals on admission is NOT correct?
items.answer: Deficient capital is credited to the partner's capital account without any cash.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Deficient capital is credited to the partner's capital account without any cash.
options: Surplus capital may be transferred to current account.
Required capital of each partner = total capital × new share.
Deficient capital is credited to the partner's capital account without any cash.
Deficiency of capital may be brought in cash.

items.stem: Lakshmi and Yash share profits 3:1. Ishaan is admitted for a 1/6 share, taken from Lakshmi and Yash in their old ratio. Their adjusted capitals are ₹2,50,000 and ₹1,20,000. Ishaan is to bring capital proportionate to Ishaan's share. Calculate Ishaan's capital.
items.markingKey: Combined capital ₹3,70,000 for 5/6 share; total capital = ₹4,44,000; Ishaan's capital = × 1/6 = ₹74,000.

items.stem: Ananya and Aditi share profits 3:2. Ananya surrenders 1/5 of Ananya's share and Aditi surrenders 1/5 of Aditi's share in favour of Shreya, the new partner. Shreya brings ₹1,25,000 as capital. After all adjustments, the capitals of Ananya and Aditi are ₹2,94,000 and ₹2,49,000. items.answer: Ananya: deficit ₹6,000 (brought in); Aditi: surplus ₹49,000 (withdrawn)
items.markingKey: New ratio 12:8:5; total capital = ₹1,25,000 ÷ 1/5 = ₹6,25,000. Required: Ananya ₹3,00,000, Aditi ₹2,00,000. Ananya deficit ₹6,000 (brought in); Aditi surplus ₹49,000 (withdrawn).

items.stem: Diya and Imran share profits 3:1. Aarav is admitted for a 1/6 share, which Aarav acquires equally from Diya and Imran. Their adjusted capitals are ₹85,000 and ₹2,10,000. Aarav is to bring capital proportionate to Aarav's share. Calculate Aarav's capital.
items.markingKey: Combined capital ₹2,95,000 for 5/6 share; total capital = ₹3,54,000; Aarav's capital = × 1/6 = ₹59,000.

items.stem: Dev and Saanvi share profits 7:3. Sneha is admitted; Sneha acquires 1/12 of the profit from Dev and 1/20 from Saanvi. Sneha brings ₹75,000 as capital. items.stem: Karthik and Gauri share profits 5:4. Priya is admitted for a 1/4 share, which Priya acquires equally from Karthik and Gauri. Their adjusted capitals are ₹1,85,000 and ₹1,90,000. Priya is to bring capital proportionate to Priya's share. Calculate Priya's capital.
items.markingKey: Combined capital ₹3,75,000 for 3/4 share; total capital = ₹5,00,000; Priya's capital = × 1/4 = ₹1,25,000.

items.stem: On the admission of a partner: (1) Stock is overvalued by ₹6,000; (2) An outstanding electricity bill of ₹3,500 is unrecorded; (3) Prepaid insurance of ₹2,000 is to be recorded. The result of revaluation is:
items.answer: Loss of ₹7,500
options: Gain of ₹2,000
Loss of ₹7,500
Gain of ₹11,500
Gain of ₹7,500

items.stem: Kavya and Diya share profits 2:3. Harpreet is admitted for a 1/6 share, taken from Kavya and Diya in their old ratio. The sacrificing ratio of Kavya and Diya is:
items.markingKey: (d) Sacrifice = old share − new share: 1/15 and 1/10 → 2:3.

items.stem: Goodwill of ₹60,000 already appears in the books when Rohan is admitted. Which journal entry records this?
items.answer: Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c
items.markingKey: (a) Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c. Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
options: Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c
Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c
New partner's Current A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs
Goodwill A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs

items.stem: Which of the following statements about goodwill is NOT correct?
items.answer: Goodwill is valued only at the time of dissolution.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: Goodwill is valued only at the time of dissolution.
options: Goodwill is valued only at the time of dissolution.
Under the capitalisation of super profit method, goodwill = super profit × 100 / normal rate of return.
Goodwill arises from the ability to earn super profits.
Goodwill is an intangible asset.

items.stem: Gauri and Om share profits 3:1. On admitting Ananya, it was agreed: (1) Building (₹3,90,000) is appreciated by 10%; (2) An outstanding electricity bill of ₹6,500 is unrecorded; (3) An unrecorded investment worth ₹7,000 is to be brought into books; (4) A provision for doubtful debts @ 10% is created on debtors of ₹40,000. Prepare the Revaluation Account and show the gain credited or debited to each old partner.
items.answer: Revaluation gain ₹35,500: Gauri ₹26,625, Om ₹8,875
items.markingKey: Items: (1) gain ₹39,000; (2) loss ₹6,500; (3) gain ₹7,000; (4) loss ₹4,000. Net gain ₹35,500 (3 marks for items), shared by old partners in old ratio 3:1: Gauri ₹26,625, Om ₹8,875 (1 mark).

items.stem: What is meant by "Normal rate of return"?
items.answer: The rate at which profit is earned by similar businesses in the same industry under normal circumstances.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The rate at which profit is earned by similar businesses in the same industry under normal circumstances.

items.stem: A provision for doubtful debts is to be created on debtors. Which side of the Revaluation Account is affected? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Debit side (loss). A new provision reduces the asset value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Debit side (loss); 2 marks for the justification: A new provision reduces the asset value.

items.stem: What is meant by "Adjusted capital"?
items.answer: A partner's capital after all adjustments for goodwill, revaluation and reserves.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A partner's capital after all adjustments for goodwill, revaluation and reserves.

items.stem: Farhan and Siddharth share profits 3:5. Riya is admitted for a 1/10 share, taken from Farhan and Siddharth in their old ratio. Goodwill of the firm is ₹2,70,000 and Riya brings the share of goodwill in cash. The premium will be credited to:
items.answer: Farhan ₹10,125, Siddharth ₹16,875
items.markingKey: (a) Premium ₹27,000 shared in sacrificing ratio 3:5.
options: Farhan ₹10,125, Siddharth ₹16,875
Farhan ₹16,875, Siddharth ₹10,125
Farhan ₹1,01,250, Siddharth ₹1,68,750
Farhan ₹13,500, Siddharth ₹13,500

items.stem: A firm has capital employed of ₹6,30,000 and an average profit of ₹87,600. The normal rate of return is 12%. Calculate goodwill by capitalising the super profit.
Calculate the goodwill of a firm at 5/2 years' purchase of the average profit of the last 4 years. Profits: 2022-23 ₹1,71,000, 2023-24 ₹1,55,000, 2024-25 ₹83,000, 2025-26 ₹67,000.

Rohan and Aryan share profits in the ratio 2:3. Lakshmi is admitted; Lakshmi acquires 1/6 of the profit from Rohan and 1/6 from Aryan. Calculate the new profit-sharing ratio and the sacrificing ratio.
items.answer: New ratio 7:13:10; sacrificing ratio 1:1
items.markingKey: New shares: Rohan 7/30, Aryan 13/30, Lakshmi 1/3 = 7:13:10 (2 marks). Sacrifice = old − new: Rohan 1/6, Aryan 1/6 = 1:1 (1 mark).

items.stem: Which of the following statements about treatment of goodwill on admission is NOT correct?
items.answer: Premium for goodwill is credited to the new partner.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Premium for goodwill is credited to the new partner.
options: Existing goodwill is written off among old partners in the old ratio.
Under AS 26, goodwill is not raised in the books on admission.
Premium for goodwill is credited to the new partner.
Premium for goodwill is credited to the sacrificing partners in the sacrificing ratio.

items.stem: What is meant by "Reconstitution of a firm"?
items.answer: A change in the existing agreement among partners, such as a change in ratio, admission, retirement or death.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: A change in the existing agreement among partners, such as a change in ratio, admission, retirement or death.

items.stem: Tanvi and Diya share profits 2:1. Sahil is admitted; Sahil acquires 1/8 of the profit from Tanvi and 1/8 from Diya. Their adjusted capitals are ₹2,70,000 and ₹1,65,000. Sahil is to bring capital proportionate to Sahil's share. Calculate Sahil's capital.
items.markingKey: Combined capital ₹4,35,000 for 3/4 share; total capital = ₹5,80,000; Sahil's capital = × 1/4 = ₹1,45,000.

items.stem: On the admission of a partner: (1) A provision for doubtful debts @ 5% is created on debtors of ₹60,000; (2) Building (₹1,20,000) is appreciated by 20%; (3) Machinery (₹2,90,000) is depreciated by 15%. The result of revaluation is:
items.answer: Loss of ₹22,500
options: Gain of ₹70,500
Gain of ₹24,000
Loss of ₹22,500
Gain of ₹22,500

items.stem: Harleen and Ishita share profits 2:3. Aisha is admitted; Aisha acquires 1/20 of the profit from Harleen and 1/10 from Ishita. The sacrificing ratio of Harleen and Ishita is:
items.markingKey: (b) Sacrifice = old share − new share: 1/20 and 1/10 → 1:2.

items.stem: Om is admitted and brings his share of goodwill in cash. Which journal entry records this?
items.answer: Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c
items.markingKey: (a) Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c. Cash brought for goodwill is first credited to Premium for Goodwill.
options: Bank A/c Dr; To Premium for Goodwill A/c
Goodwill A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs
Old partners' Capital A/cs Dr; To Goodwill A/c
New partner's Current A/c Dr; To Old partners' Capital A/cs

items.stem: Which of the following statements about goodwill is NOT correct?
items.answer: Self-generated goodwill is recorded in the books under AS 26.
items.markingKey: (c) Incorrect statement: Self-generated goodwill is recorded in the books under AS 26.
options: Goodwill arises from the ability to earn super profits.
Goodwill is an intangible asset.
Self-generated goodwill is recorded in the books under AS 26.
Under the capitalisation of super profit method, goodwill = super profit × 100 / normal rate of return.

items.stem: Rohan and Ishita share profits 1:1. On admitting Mehak, it was agreed: (1) An outstanding electricity bill of ₹6,500 is unrecorded; (2) Machinery (₹1,10,000) is depreciated by 5%; (3) A provision for doubtful debts @ 10% is created on debtors of ₹1,90,000; (4) Building (₹3,80,000) is appreciated by 10%; (5) An unrecorded investment worth ₹19,000 is to be brought into books. Prepare the Revaluation Account and show the gain credited or debited to each old partner.
items.answer: Revaluation gain ₹26,000: Rohan ₹13,000, Ishita ₹13,000
items.markingKey: Items: (1) loss ₹6,500; (2) loss ₹5,500; (3) loss ₹19,000; (4) gain ₹38,000; (5) gain ₹19,000. Net gain ₹26,000 (3 marks for items), shared by old partners in old ratio 1:1: Rohan ₹13,000, Ishita ₹13,000 (1 mark).

items.stem: What is meant by "Super profit"?
items.answer: The excess of the average actual profit over the normal profit of a business.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The excess of the average actual profit over the normal profit of a business.
